- Definition
	- Respiratory impairment from submersion/immersion in liquid

- Avoid terms:
	- “Near-drowning”
	- “Secondary drowning”
	- “Wet drowning”
	- Terms do not alter management

- Consider underlying cause
	- Seizure
	- Hypoglycaemia
	- Arrhythmia / long QT
	- Intoxication

- Investigations
	- Not required
		- Asymptomatic + alert child

	- Indications
		- Guided by history + examination

	- Key points
	- Chest X-ray
		- Poor outcome correlation

	- Altered mental state without hypoxia
		- Hypothermia
		- TBI
		- Hypoglycaemia
		- Co-existing illness

	- ECG
		- Arrhythmias
		- Long QT syndrome

- Management
	- Positioning
		- Vomiting common → aspiration risk
		- Spontaneously breathing
			- Lateral/recovery position

	- Antibiotics
		- No prophylaxis
		- Indications
			- Infection/sepsis
			- Grossly contaminated water

- Hypothermia
	- Common complication
	- Initial management
		- Remove wet clothes
		- Dry child
		- Minimise exposure
	- Active warming
		- Indications
			- Temp <34°C
			- No brain injury
		- Methods
			- Warm IV fluids
			- Humidified oxygen
			- Forced-air warming
	- Special situation
		- Therapeutic hypothermia
			- Possible benefit in hypoxic brain injury
			- Discuss with PICU/intensivist
- paediatric consultation indications
	- Increased work of breathing
	- SpO₂ <95%
	- Abnormal respiratory exam
	- Suspected underlying cause

- Transfer indications
	- Persistent altered consciousness
	- Respiratory failure
	- Ongoing hypoxia
 
- Discharge criteria (all required)
	- Observed ≥8 hours
	- Asymptomatic
	- Normal respiratory exam
	- SpO₂ ≥95%
	- Water safety education completed
	- No safety concerns
	- Social work review if needed

- poor prognosis
	- Submersion >5 min
	- BLS delay >10 min
	- CPR ongoing on arrival
	- GCS <5
	- Temperature <30°C
	- pH <7.1
